title: Search a 2D Matrix
statement: A grid of integers has two promises: each row is sorted left to right, and the first number of every row is bigger than the last number of the row above. Say whether a target value appears anywhere in the grid, in log time.

example.caption: Read the rows one after another and you get a single sorted line. Target 11 is in the middle row.

idea.sentence: Because each row continues where the last one ended, the whole grid is one sorted line. Binary search it, and turn each flat index back into a row and column.

jargon.plain: Read a grid row by row as one long array. Here we only pretend to do it: nothing is copied.
In a grid with cols columns, flat index i sits at row i / cols (rounded down) and column i % cols.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: a matrix and a target, e.g. [[1,3,5,7],[10,11,16,20],[23,30,34,60]] and 11

rows.name: Binary search on the flat line
rows.note: The line has m * n items, and each look halves it. Nothing is copied: only the index maths changes.

fast.takeaway: You do not need two searches. One binary search over m * n virtual items, plus a divide and a remainder, is enough.

stages.title: One virtual line
stages.note: l = 0 and r = rows * cols - 1. The matrix is never copied.

stages.title: Middle to cell
stages.note: Take the middle flat index m, then row = m / cols and col = m % cols.

stages.title: Drop a half
stages.note: Too small: l = m + 1. Too big: r = m - 1.

stages.title: Answer
stages.note: The cell equals the target: return true. If l passes r, every cell was ruled out: return false.

edges.title: Single cell
edges.why: rows * cols is 1, so l = r = 0 and the middle is the only cell.

edges.title: One row
edges.why: With one row, row is always 0 and the search is a plain binary search.

edges.title: One column
edges.why: cols is 1, so row = m and col = 0. Dividing by cols still works.

edges.title: Between two rows
edges.why: 4 sits between the end of row 0 and the start of row 1. A flat search just runs out of range.

gotchas.text: m / cols is a float in JS. Use Math.floor(m / cols), otherwise matrix[1.5] is undefined and the next index throws.
Check len(matrix) == 0 before reading matrix[0], or an empty input panics with index out of range.
Divide by the number of columns, not rows. Mixing them up works on square grids and fails on 3 by 4.
Do not build the flat array to search it. That costs O(m * n) and throws away the point of binary search.

recap.pattern: Binary search on a virtual flat array
recap.key: A grid whose rows chain in order is one sorted line. Search 0..m*n-1 and map each index to row = i / n, col = i % n.
moves: Set l = 0 and r = rows * cols - 1
Take m, then row = m / cols and col = m % cols
Compare matrix[row][col] with the target and drop a half
